intro.say: Moving and playing make your body happy and strong!

rounds.say: Running, jumping, dancing and climbing are all exercise. Exercise makes your body strong!
rounds.caption: Move every day

rounds.say: After playing, your body needs rest. Sitting quietly and sleeping help you feel good again.
rounds.caption: Play, then rest

rounds.explain: Riding a bike moves your whole body.
Lying in bed lets your body rest.

rounds.ask: How does exercise make your body?

options.label: Weak
options.why: Exercise makes you stronger, not weaker.

rounds.explain: Moving makes your muscles, heart and bones strong.

rounds.ask: You played tag a long time and feel tired. What helps?

options.label: Run even more
options.why: Your body needs a break first.

rounds.explain: Resting gives your body time to feel better.
Some things get us moving, others let us rest. We need both!

intro.say: Sleep helps your body grow and your brain get ready for a new day.

rounds.say: While you sleep, your body grows and fixes itself. Your brain sorts out what you learned today.
rounds.caption: Sleep helps me grow

rounds.say: Children your age need lots of sleep, about 10 to 12 hours every night! That is much more than grown-ups.
rounds.caption: About 10–12 hours

rounds.ask: How many hours of sleep do children your age need?
rounds.explain: Children need about 10 to 12 hours of sleep each night.

rounds.ask: What happens to your body while you sleep?

options.label: It floats
options.why: You stay in bed, don't worry.

rounds.explain: Your body grows and repairs itself while you sleep.

options.label: Playing on a tablet
options.why: Bright screens can keep you awake.

rounds.explain: A calm story helps your body get ready to sleep.

rounds.ask: Tom stayed up very late. How might he feel tomorrow?

options.label: Super full of energy
options.why: Without sleep we usually feel tired.

rounds.explain: Not enough sleep makes us feel tired and grumpy.

rounds.ask: Put the bedtime routine in order.
rounds.explain: Get clean, put on pyjamas, hear a calm story in bed, and then drift off to sleep.

intro.say: Let's plan a healthy day with the right mix of moving, eating, drinking and sleeping.

rounds.say: Children should be active for at least one hour every day. Exercise that makes you a little out of breath is great for your heart.
rounds.caption: 1 hour of play a day

rounds.say: When you exercise you get hot and sweaty, so drink water. Then rest and sleep well to be ready for tomorrow.
rounds.caption: Move · Drink · Sleep

rounds.ask: How much active play should children have each day?
rounds.explain: At least one hour of active play every day keeps you healthy.

rounds.ask: You ran a race and feel hot. What should you drink?

options.label: Fizzy drink
options.why: Fizzy drinks have lots of sugar.

rounds.explain: Water cools you down and replaces the water you sweated out.

rounds.ask: Why does your body sweat when you exercise?

options.label: It is raining
options.why: Sweat comes from your skin, not rain.

options.label: To change colour
options.why: Sweat does not change your colour.

rounds.explain: Sweat helps cool your hot body down.

rounds.ask: Mia slept 11 hours, Max slept 6 hours. Who had a better amount of sleep?

options.label: Max
options.why: 6 hours is too little for a child.

rounds.explain: Mia slept 11 hours, which is right for a child.

options.label: TV all day
options.why: Sitting all day is not good for your body.

options.label: Sweets and stay up late
options.why: Sugar and late nights make us tired.

rounds.explain: A good day mixes play, healthy food and plenty of sleep.

rounds.ask: Put this healthy day in order.
rounds.explain: Breakfast gives energy for play, dinner comes in the evening, then a good sleep.
